solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: New dawn breaks very pale in due course (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.New: a new version of the word, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.breaks: the rearranged letters break into the other word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: ashen = very pale, grey-faced; it is split open
DAWN rearranged, sitting between AS and HEN

annotation.surface: A new day breaks, grey and pale, as it will in the fullness of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New dawn breaks' reads as a sunrise; 'New' works on DAWN, and 'breaks' pushes the result into ASHEN.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'as and when' means at whatever time something happens, which is in due course.

entries.clue: Jelly equally still? (5)

blocks.note: as = equally, as in 'as tall'
a still is a photograph, a pic

annotation.surface: A question whether a jelly is just as motionless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about the wobbling jelly; it is a noun, a single frame or photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: aspic is a clear savoury jelly set from meat or fish stock.

entries.clue: Help, having bought sweet with a minor defect? (5-5,7)

blocks.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the sweet course
as written
minor = lesser
a vice is a moral defect

annotation.surface: Someone who bought a slightly faulty sweet asks for help.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'minor defect' as one idea, a small flaw; it splits in two, and 'sweet' calls for the British slang word for pudding. The definition covers the help owed once you have bought.
annotation.definitionFit: After-sales service is the help a shop gives you once you have bought something.

entries.clue: Abandon taking bath to fight minister’s case (8,3)

indicatorNotes.taking: the first word takes the second inside it

blocks.note: to ditch = to abandon
a spa is a bath, as in the city of Bath's spa; it goes inside DITCH
to box = to fight

annotation.surface: Someone gives up bathing to go and fight a minister's legal case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks legal, a lawsuit to fight; it is a physical box. The dispatch box is a British minister's red case, also the lectern box in the Commons.
annotation.definitionFit: A dispatch box is the red case that carries a British minister's official papers.

entries.clue: Answer for European found in port and a cigar (6)

indicatorNotes.for: 'for' in the sense of 'in exchange for': A is swapped in and E goes out
indicatorNotes.found in: the swap happens inside the word for port

blocks.note: a haven is a harbour, a port
A (answer) replaces E (European) in HAVEN
the A as written, added on

annotation.surface: A reply offered in place of a European, found in a harbour with a cigar.
annotation.walkthrough: A = answer and E = European are standard abbreviations. The answer is also a port city, which makes 'port' look like the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A Havana is a cigar from Cuba, named after its capital.

entries.clue: Neither partner has married in the interim, as is customary (8)

indicatorNotes.in the interim: in the gap between the two words, so M sits between them

blocks.note: neither … nor; the partner word of neither
m. = married, as in genealogy
an ally is a partner

annotation.surface: Neither partner has wed anyone else meanwhile, which is how it usually goes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about a couple's fidelity; 'in the interim' is really a placement, the gap between two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what happens normally happens by custom, as is customary.

entries.clue: In hearing, summon witness (5)

indicatorNotes.In hearing: within someone's hearing a word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: to cite a witness is to summon them to court; say it out loud

annotation.surface: At a court hearing, the lawyer calls a witness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court hearing, which fits 'summon witness'; it is the homophone signal, and 'witness' is the definition, a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to sight a ship or a suspect is to see it, to witness it.
annotation.definitionNote: witness here is a verb, to see, matching SIGHT as a verb

entries.clue: Fast driver in MG flipped during prison escape? (8,4)

indicatorNotes.flipped: turned over, so MG reads backwards
indicatorNotes.during: IN and the flipped MG go inside the word for escape

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison
as written; it and GM go inside LOSS
MG, the British car make, backwards
an escape of heat or gas is a loss

annotation.surface: A speedster in an MG rolls over while fleeing jail.
annotation.walkthrough: Stirling Moss was a British racing driver of the 1950s. The MG in the surface is his car; in the wordplay it is just two letters to turn round.
annotation.definitionFit: Stirling Moss was one of Britain's great Formula One drivers, so a fast driver.

entries.clue: Crew with outfits on start motoring (3,2,5)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, 'on' puts the second part above the first

blocks.note: get-ups are outfits, often eccentric ones
a crew is a team

annotation.surface: A team, dressed in their kit, sets off in their cars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crew with outfits' seems to describe a costumed team; in the wordplay the outfits are stacked on top of the crew. The phrase comes from firing up a steam engine.
annotation.definitionFit: To get up steam is to build power before moving, so to start motoring.

entries.clue: Dry until spring, mainly (5)

indicatorNotes.mainly: the main part of the word, all but its last letter

blocks.note: until = to, as in 'nine to five'
a well is a spring of water; drop its last letter

annotation.surface: Weather that stays dry until spring, mostly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dry' reads as weather, an adjective; it is a verb, to dry yourself.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb made from the noun: rubbing yourself with a bath towel is how you dry off.

entries.clue: Stand on the pavement to kiss premier (3,4)

blocks.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
premier = first, top

annotation.surface: Someone stands on the pavement waiting to kiss the prime minister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a place where buses stand. 'Premier' looks like a prime minister and means only top.
annotation.definitionFit: A bus stop is a stand at the kerb where buses halt.

entries.clue: Bandy ball made from wood covered in white and yellow (3-6)

blocks.note: a bowl is the wooden ball of the lawn game bowls
egg white and yolk; egged = pelted with eggs

annotation.surface: A wooden ball splattered with white and yellow, being knocked about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bandy' looks like a verb, to hit a ball back and forth, which fits the ball; it is an adjective, curved outwards at the knees.
annotation.definitionFit: Bandy legs curve outwards, so bandy means bow-legged.

entries.clue: Second Snickers editor took out to eat (11)

blocks.note: s = second
snickers are sniggers, bursts of laughter
ed. = editor

annotation.surface: An editor takes a second Snickers bar out to eat.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Snickers' the chocolate bar, which suits 'to eat'; lower-case, snickers are giggles.
annotation.definitionFit: Animals are slaughtered, killed or taken out, so they can be eaten.

entries.clue: Pharoah is northerly African (5)

indicatorNotes.northerly: heading north, so upwards in a down answer, which turns the word round

blocks.note: Tut, short for Tutankhamun
IS read upwards

annotation.surface: A pharaoh is from the north of Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: Egypt's pharaohs really were northerly Africans, which is why the surface works; the answer is from Central Africa.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so an African.

entries.clue: Irrational price appropriate in creative spheres? (6)

blocks.note: pi is an irrational number
a rate is a price, as in a going rate

annotation.surface: An unreasonable fee that seems fitting in artistic circles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective, fitting; it is a verb, to take without permission. 'Spheres' nods to pi and circles.
annotation.definitionFit: To pirate is to appropriate someone's creative work, such as music or films, without paying.

entries.clue: Trump now binding university with billions? (5)

indicatorNotes.binding: wrapping round, so U goes inside

blocks.note: pots of money = billions, a great deal
U = university; it goes inside POTS

annotation.surface: Trump is now tying a university to billions of dollars.
annotation.walkthrough: POTUS is the acronym for President of the United States, the office Trump holds at the time of this puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: Trump now holds the office of POTUS, the US President.

entries.clue: Remote ref effectively new troublemaker (7)

blocks.note: VAR, the video assistant referee in football, reviews play from a remote room
in mint condition = brand new

annotation.surface: A video referee is, in effect, the new villain of football.
annotation.walkthrough: VAR is the Video Assistant Referee, football's off-pitch replay official. A varmint is a rascal.
annotation.definitionFit: A varmint, from vermin, is a pest or mischievous troublemaker.

entries.clue: Impressive feature of court holding with truth and right (3,6)

indicatorNotes.holding: the first word holds the next pieces inside it

blocks.note: to court is to woo; it holds W and FACT
w = with
a truth is a fact
r = right

annotation.surface: A grand feature of a law court, joined with truth and justice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court or a palace; it is a verb, to woo, wrapped round W and FACT.
annotation.definitionFit: A wow factor is the quality that impresses at first sight.

entries.clue: Turning grass in dock, one creates division (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Turning: turned round, so LAWN reads backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the turned word goes inside the word for dock

blocks.note: to dock is to cut short, to curtail
LAWN backwards, placed before CURTAIL's last L

annotation.surface: A mower turning over the grass on a dockside, marking out a boundary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a quay or a weed; it is a verb, to cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: A curtain wall is a wall that divides or encloses, as between a castle's towers.

entries.clue: Invisible force teleports GI elsewhere (11)

indicatorNotes.elsewhere: the letters are put in other places

blocks.note: the eleven letters of TELEPORTS GI rearranged

annotation.surface: An unseen power beams an American soldier somewhere else.
annotation.walkthrough: A GI is an American soldier; here it is just two letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is an unseen spirit that throws things about, an invisible force.

entries.clue: Stiffen masonry structure faced with stone (6)

indicatorNotes.faced with: given a front, so ST comes first

blocks.note: st = stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
an arch is built of masonry

annotation.surface: Strengthening a masonry structure by facing it with stone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all building work, so 'Stiffen' suggests reinforcing a wall; it is what you do to a collar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: laundry starch makes collars and shirts stiff.

entries.clue: Donkey’s saddle, harness etc placed under small chimney (10)

indicatorNotes.placed under: in a down answer, the rest sits below S

blocks.note: s = small
moke is British slang for a donkey, plus the 's
tack is the saddle, bridle and harness of a horse

annotation.surface: A donkey's saddle and harness are stowed beneath a little chimney.
annotation.walkthrough: The saddle and harness are a list in the surface; together they are TACK, the riders' word for such gear.
annotation.definitionFit: A smokestack is a tall chimney, as on a factory or steamship.

entries.clue: Drifters work out what to do with four letters from the 11th (8)

blocks.note: to work out = to plan

blocks.clueFragment: what to do with four letters from the 11th
blocks.note: K is the 11th letter; the four letters from it run K to N

annotation.surface: Aimless wanderers trying to decide what to do from the 11th of the month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The 11th' looks like a date; it is the 11th letter of the alphabet, K, and the four letters K, L, M, N are written 'K to N'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny organisms that drift with the ocean currents.

entries.clue: Most foul new fizz is from France (8)

blocks.note: n = new
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
est is French for 'is'

annotation.surface: A dreadful new sparkling wine turns out to be French.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is from France' seems to say where the fizz comes from; it asks for the French word for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: foul and nasty both mean very unpleasant, here in the superlative.

entries.clue: Gangster’s guns passing through Long Island millionaire (6)

blocks.note: gat is old gangster slang for a gun
by = via, passing through

annotation.surface: Mobsters' weapons travel through the home of a Long Island millionaire.
annotation.walkthrough: Jay Gatsby is the rich host in F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby, set on Long Island; he was himself linked to gangsters.
annotation.definitionFit: Gatsby is the fictional millionaire of Long Island's West Egg.

entries.clue: Privately consider bloodshed abominable (6,6,5)

indicatorNotes.abominable: in a dreadful state, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the seventeen letters of CONSIDER BLOODSHED rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone secretly finds violence detestable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Privately consider' reads as one phrase, to think something to yourself; 'Privately' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: things done where the doors are shut are done in private, out of public view.

entries.clue: Sons notice warm colour turning more blue (6)

indicatorNotes.turning: turned round, so RED reads backwards

blocks.note: s = son, in family trees
an ad is a notice in a paper
RED backwards

annotation.surface: Boys see a warm red turning a deeper blue.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about colours, so 'blue' looks like a shade; it means sad.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: feeling blue means feeling down, so more blue compares low spirits.

entries.clue: See sandwiches are discontinued in Lidl? Very well (10)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the first word goes either side of the rest, like bread
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so END goes inside the shop's name

blocks.note: to spy = to see; it sandwiches the rest
the supermarket name as written
things that are discontinued end; it goes inside LIDL after the first L

annotation.surface: A shopper spots that sandwiches have been dropped from Lidl, and is quite happy about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Lidl is a German discount supermarket chain; here its name is simply four letters that END is slipped into.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'splendid' is old-fashioned praise, so doing splendidly is doing very well.

entries.clue: Boss recovered from effects of rude fellow (8)

blocks.note: you are over an illness when you have recovered from it
a bear is a gruff, ill-mannered man

annotation.surface: A boss has got over the effects of a rude colleague.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as a noun, the manager in the surface; it is a verb, to boss about.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to overbear others is to domineer, pushing them about.

entries.clue: Converting madrasa, bishop’s role with mission (14)

indicatorNotes.Converting: changing the form of the letters, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the fourteen letters of MADRASA BISHOPS rearranged

annotation.surface: A bishop's missionary task of converting an Islamic school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Converting' and 'mission' paint religious conversion; the mission is a diplomatic one. A madrasa is an Islamic school.
annotation.definitionFit: An ambassadorship is the post of heading a diplomatic mission.

entries.clue: Compact prisoner studies echo (8)

blocks.note: a con is a convict
a den is a study, a private room
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A tight little cell where an inmate's study echoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Compact' reads as an adjective; it is a verb, to pack tighter. 'Studies' is a noun, rooms, not reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean pressing something into less space.

entries.clue: Queen’s favourite taking part in Charles’s execution? (5)

indicatorNotes.taking part in: the answer is part of the words that follow

blocks.note: CharlESS EXecution

annotation.surface: Was the queen's darling involved in the beheading of Charles I?
annotation.walkthrough: The Earl of Essex was Elizabeth I's favourite, and was himself executed. Charles I's execution came decades later, so the surface is a false lead.
annotation.definitionFit: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, was Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.

entries.clue: Likely to drop off fencing equipment to the front yard (6)

indicatorNotes.to the front: read towards the front, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a sword is fencing kit; SWORD backwards
y = yard

annotation.surface: Fencing gear is liable to fall off when moved to the front yard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests garden fences in the yard; it is the sport of swordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sleepy person is nodding and likely to fall asleep at any moment.

entries.clue: Reserve I had to replace centre for variety (10)

indicatorNotes.to replace: ID goes in instead of the centre letters

blocks.note: variety = difference
the two middle letters of DIFFERENCE, taken out
I'd = I had, put in their place

annotation.surface: A reserve player says he had to replace the centre for a change.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like team sport, with a reserve replacing the centre; 'Reserve' is the definition, meaning shyness.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: reserve in a person means shyness and holding back.

entries.clue: Passionate short film opens with fine hero getting stripped off (6)

indicatorNotes.opens with: the film word comes after the other pieces

blocks.note: f = fine, on pencil grades
HERO without its first and last letters
vid, short for video

annotation.surface: A steamy short film begins with a handsome hero taking his clothes off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' in the surface is undressing; in the wordplay it removes HERO's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: fervid, from Latin for glowing hot, means burning with feeling.

entries.clue: Reckon mixture of red and cyan figures at a ceilidh? (7,5)

indicatorNotes.mixture of: a mixture is things stirred together, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: to reckon is to count
RED CYAN rearranged; 'and' joins the two colours

annotation.surface: Working out a blend of red and cyan for the costumes at a Scottish dance.
annotation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish evening of folk dancing, where dances are made of set figures. 'Figures' looks like numbers to reckon.
annotation.definitionFit: A country dance is a folk dance made of set figures, the staple of a ceilidh.

entries.clue: Tiny bug one step behind rats in retreat (10)

indicatorNotes.in retreat: going back, so DRAT reads backwards
indicatorNotes.behind: the other pieces come after it

blocks.note: 'rats!' is an oath like DRAT; backwards
I = one
a grade is a step on a scale

annotation.surface: A little insect falls a step behind rats as they flee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like the rodents; it is the exclamation, the same as 'drat!'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tardigrade, or water bear, is a microscopic animal, loosely a tiny bug.

entries.clue: Yankee hit hard in worse Australian fraud (11)

indicatorNotes.in: Y and WHACK go inside the word for worse

blocks.note: iller = more ill, worse
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
to whack = to hit hard

annotation.surface: An American gets beaten up in an even worse Australian scam.
annotation.walkthrough: An illywhacker is Australian slang for a con man, known from Peter Carey's novel Illywhacker.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Australian slang for a confidence trickster, a con man who defrauds people.

entries.clue: Tanker with late British figurehead on front of ship (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, the first piece comes after the one it sits on

blocks.note: the bows are the front of a ship
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

annotation.surface: A tanker carries the carved figure of a late British monarch on its prow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figurehead' suggests the carved figure on a ship's prow; here it is the Queen as head of state. A bowser is a British word for a fuel or water tanker.
annotation.definitionFit: A bowser is a tanker truck for fuel or water.

entries.clue: Church cushion covers measured using feet (5)

indicatorNotes.covers: the second word goes round the first

blocks.note: CE = Church of England
a pad is a cushion; it covers CE

annotation.surface: Church kneelers' covers were measured with feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' reads as a noun, cushion covers; it is a verb, the cushion wrapping round the church. CE is the Church of England.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal description: walking a room out heel to toe measures it with your feet.

entries.clue: Yearly benefit American’s behind, performing show stopper? (5,6)

blocks.note: p.a. = per annum, yearly
use = benefit, as in 'what's the use?'
butt is American for backside
an actor performing is on

annotation.surface: An annual allowance for a US performer's backside, the highlight of the show.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'show stopper' is normally a sensational act; read literally it is the button that stops a TV show.
annotation.definitionFit: A pause button stops a show you are watching, literally a show stopper.

entries.clue: Youth trained to fight scoundrel had heart, you’d say (5,5)

indicatorNotes.you’d say: what you would say is the spoken sound, so the words are judged by ear

blocks.note: a cad is a scoundrel
had = ate, heart = core; in British speech ATE is often said 'et', and CORPS is said 'core'

annotation.surface: A scoundrel who was a young soldier once had courage, so they say.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heart' reads as courage; it is the core, as of an apple, and 'had' is ate. CORPS drops its P and S in speech.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: this school or youth unit gives teenagers military training.

entries.clue: Hot meal star wheels outside for Neville, taking veg out first (6,3,5)

indicatorNotes.first: this piece is placed at the front
indicatorNotes.outside: only the outside letters of the name are used

blocks.note: to veg out = to chill, relax
a star is an icon
wheels is slang for a car
the outer letters of NevillE

annotation.surface: A star serves Neville a hot meal on a trolley, having left the vegetables out first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Veg' looks like vegetables to leave out of the dish; 'veg out' is slang for relaxing, which is CHILL, the piece placed first.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the chillies make this stew of mince and beans a hot meal in both senses.

entries.clue: Clipper shaved Katy’s last bit of hair off (5,4)

indicatorNotes.last bit of: the last bit of a word is its final letter, the only one taken
indicatorNotes.off: gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: shaved = cut

blocks.clueFragment: Katy’s last bit of hair off
blocks.note: KATYS plus R, the last letter of hair, rearranged

annotation.surface: A pair of clippers shaved off the last of Katy's hair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' looks like hair clippers; it is a fast sailing ship. The Cutty Sark is the tea clipper preserved at Greenwich, London.
annotation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is a famous 19th-century tea clipper.

entries.clue: Using some radios, uni scientists inverted wave form (8)

indicatorNotes.Using some: only some of the letters are used, so the answer sits inside
indicatorNotes.inverted: turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run through raDIOS, UNI Scientists; read them from the end

annotation.surface: University scientists invert a radio wave, using some of their sets.
annotation.walkthrough: Radios and scientists make 'wave form' sound like physics lab talk, which it is; the definition hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A sinusoid is the smooth wave shape of a sine curve.

entries.clue: Dogs perhaps upset by high-pitched noise on a walk? (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: tipped up, so in a down answer the word reads upwards

blocks.note: dogs are pets; PETS upwards
a ping is a sharp high sound

annotation.surface: Dogs on a walk get upset by a shrill whistle.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog walk makes 'on a walk' sound like part of the scene; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, marked by the question mark: a walk is a series of steps.

entries.clue: Plover’s cry coming from behind that object (6)

indicatorNotes.coming from behind: read from the back, so WEEP runs backwards

blocks.note: to weep is to cry; WEEP backwards
it = that object

annotation.surface: A bird's call rings out from behind something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plover's cry' looks like the definition, since peewit is the bird's call; but 'cry' is needed for WEEP, so the definition is 'Plover' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: The peewit, or lapwing, is a plover named after its call.

entries.clue: Curse CEO for one estimate (8)

blocks.note: a CEO is one example of an exec, an executive
to rate is to estimate

annotation.surface: A curse on the chief executive for one bad forecast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For one' marks CEO as an example of EXEC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin for putting under a curse, it means to denounce or damn.

entries.clue: Anti-establishment view in this newspaper’s unknown (6)

blocks.note: in this newspaper = here; with the 's, HERE'S
y is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: A dissenting opinion in this paper's columns comes from an anonymous writer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In this newspaper' reads as a location in the surface; it simply means 'here'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: originally belief against the established church, now any view against orthodoxy.

entries.clue: Make a pariah lance 100 boils (6)

blocks.note: LANCE plus C (100 in Roman numerals), rearranged

annotation.surface: An outcast has to lance a hundred boils.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boils' reads as a noun, sores to lance; it is a verb, the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To cancel someone, in the modern sense, is to shun them, making them a pariah.

entries.clue: Second person who heard hail (3-3)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is known only by its sound, so the spelling may differ

blocks.note: you is the second person pronoun; you + who, said aloud

annotation.surface: Asking who was the second person to hear someone call.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second person' reads as another person; it is the grammatical second person, YOU.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection: it is the cry used to attract someone's attention across a distance.

entries.clue: A typical COP vacillates, suggesting dire consequences (11)

indicatorNotes.vacillates: wavers back and forth, so the letters move about

blocks.note: the eleven letters of A TYPICAL COP rearranged

annotation.surface: A typical COP climate summit dithers, hinting at disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: COP is the UN's annual climate conference; the surface is a fair jibe about climate warnings.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Apocalypse is the end of the world, so such warnings foretell doom.

entries.clue: Greek theatre, oh God, in Latin (5)

blocks.note: O = oh
Deum, as in Te Deum, is Latin for God

annotation.surface: A Greek play in which someone cries 'O God' in Latin.
annotation.walkthrough: DEUM is the object form of Latin Deus, familiar from the hymn Te Deum.
annotation.definitionFit: An odeum is a roofed theatre for music in ancient Greece.

entries.clue: Sufficient power? Little elevator given half of that (5)

blocks.note: a golf tee raises the ball a little
the first two letters of THAT

annotation.surface: Is there enough power in a small lift given half of that?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little elevator' reads as a small lift; it is a golf tee, which holds the ball up.
annotation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has enough power to enforce itself.

entries.clue: Letter Wilde wrote for fun in D Wing taken the wrong way (2,9)

indicatorNotes.in: PRO FUN goes inside the reversed wing
indicatorNotes.taken the wrong way: turned round, so SIDE runs backwards

blocks.note: as written
a wing is a side; SIDE backwards, split open
pro = for
as written; PRO FUN goes after the E of EDIS

annotation.walkthrough: De Profundis is the long letter Oscar Wilde wrote in Reading Gaol, so 'D Wing' paints the prison truthfully.

entries.clue: Women’s retail stores expand (5)

indicatorNotes.stores: keeps inside, so W goes inside SELL

blocks.note: w = women
to retail is to sell; it stores W

annotation.surface: Women's clothing shops are growing.
